NASA satellites just caught underwater volcanic eruptions expanding the beaches of Surtsey, but what if these eruptions never stopped? As magma cools against seawater, it hardens into brand-new basalt rock. If Pacific volcanoes erupted continuously, shallow ocean floors could rise above sea level, slowly stitching isolated islands into massive new landmasses. Ocean currents would shift dramatically, changing global climate patterns while expanding coastlines by miles every year. Would you explore a brand-new volcanic continent? Follow for more what-ifs.
